meta.title: Consolation, S.172 No.1
meta.source_credit: Score edition: Ryan Prince and the Mutopia Project (piece 1654), CC BY 3.0. Composition public domain.
meta.notation_notes: 25 bars of 4/4 from quarter 0, no pickup: bars 1–3, 5–7, 17–19, 21–23 begin with a quarter rest in the chord layer (off-beat chords). Final bar sounds three quarters (held chord). Score reconstructed from the Mutopia MIDI render (CC BY 3.0, Ryan Prince / Mutopia Project); no CC64 in the source. Single tempo 60 from the MIDI (the draft value 100 was wrong). Bar 12 beat 4.5–5: D♯5/F♯5 grace-length notes into bar 13. MIDI pitches are enharmonically neutral; F𝄪 (MIDI G) and A♯ (MIDI B♭) spellings are editorial. MIDI-derived edition, not a critical edition.

summary: A 25-bar hymn in E major. A chorale of off-beat chords over a held inner B (bars 1–4) is repeated under a tolling top B (5–8) and turned by an A♯ø7 pivot toward G♯ minor. The middle (9–16) is a two-bar sighing figure, i6/4–VI6–V7, stated twice in G♯ minor and then slid a semitone down into G major; a C7 heard as a German sixth leads back to E in 6/4 position (17). The closing phrase leans on IV over a falling bass and ends with a V11–V7–I cadence with G♯ on top.

sections.name: Chorale statement (E)
sections.description: Off-beat chords over an inner B pedal; I–ii–I6–vi7–V/V–V7.

sections.name: Theme over tolling B
sections.description: Bars 1–3 repeated with B4 on every strong beat; A♯ø7 turns to D♯7 (V of G♯ minor).

sections.name: Middle: G♯ minor → G major
sections.description: Two-bar sigh (i6/4–VI6–V7) stated twice in G♯ minor, then a semitone lower in G major; German sixth returns to E.

sections.name: Return
sections.description: Bars 5–8 return over B bass (I6/4); V9/V–V7 cadence into bar 21.

sections.name: Closing phrase
sections.description: E7/D–A/C♯ tonicizes IV; bass descends to B1; V11–V7–I with G♯ on top.

tricks: Bars 1–7: inner B2/B3 sounds in every chord while the bass moves; the dominant pedal makes ii and I6 blur into one calm sound.
Bars 5–8: the same chords with only a repeated top B4 added on the strong beats; a melody made from one note.
Bar 7: one altered note (A♯ for B) turns vi7 into A♯ø7 and pivots to G♯ minor.
Bars 9–16: a two-bar figure moved down a semitone (G♯ minor → G major) by sliding D♯7 to G/D.
Bar 16: C7 respelt as a German sixth (C–E–G–A♯) brings E back in 6/4 position, so the return arrives softly.
Bar 21: D♮ in the bass (E7/D) tilts the close toward IV before the final cadence.

loop_candidates.why: V7 at the end of bar 4 resolves to E at bar 1; off-beat chords leave the downbeat free for a kick.
i6/4–VI6–V7 in G♯ minor; D♯7 returns to G♯m/D♯ as in bar 11.
Same figure in G major (I6/4–vi6–V7), returning as in bar 15.

hook_candidates.why: Tolling B4 on beats 1 and 3 over off-beat chords.
E5–D♯5 sigh with the chromatic run back up.
German sixth sliding into E in 6/4 position.

kpop_uses.why: Bars 1–4 loop as a soft off-beat piano bed for a ballad verse.
Bars 7–8: A♯ø7–D♯7 lifts toward the relative minor key area.
Bars 9–16: the minor sigh and its semitone drop into G give a bridge a key change downward.
Bars 17–21: return with the German-sixth approach; there is no key lift in the source, the release comes from the cadence.
